summary: Iteration-4 focused testing on the new File & media storage feature (turf photo uploads). Backend: 12/12 pytest tests pass covering POST /api/owner/uploads (auth required 401, non-image rejected 400, happy-path path under goturf/turfs/{owner_id}/ with url=/api/media/<path>), GET /api/media/{path} (200 public no-auth with correct image bytes + content-type and Cache-Control:public, 403 for goturf/verifications/ prefix, 403 for other prefixes, 403/404 for path traversal '..'), /files regression (401 without token), owner create-turf-with-image happy path (persisted + visible on GET /turfs/{id}), owner payout-method POST momo regression (200). Frontend Playwright: logged in owner@goturf.gh via /auth (login-email/login-password/login-submit), navigated via owner-tab-turfs, opened add-turf-btn dialog, uploaded a 1x1 PNG through hidden turf-image-input, thumbnail + remove-image-0 appeared, img src is the absolute https URL to /api/media/goturf/turfs/{owner_id}/<uuid>.png. Filled turf-name, turf-hood, turf-type (plain input), turf-base=200, clicked save-turf → new turf 'TEST_ITER4_UI_<ts>' appears in My Turfs with its /api/media/... image, and the same image renders on the public Home grid. Zero console errors during the flow.

minor.issue: Content-type is trusted entirely from the client (f.content_type). A client can set image/png on arbitrary bytes and bypass the type gate. Consider sniffing magic bytes (e.g., imghdr/PIL) and/or validating extension vs. sniffed type.

Size check is per-file but there is no cap on total files per request, nor on cumulative size. A caller can POST many 6MB files in one request. Add max files-per-request (e.g., 10) and per-user rate limiting.

Entire file is read into memory with await f.read() before size check. For a 6MB cap this is fine, but it means a client sending a 100MB stream is fully buffered before the 400 is returned. Consider streaming with an incremental size check.

Public endpoint has no rate limiting and no object-exists check before get_object (which just 404s on exception). Fine, but add explicit 404 on NoSuchKey vs. 500 on other backend errors for easier debugging.
Returned 405 in cleanup (no delete route). Not a regression — just noting the owner cannot delete a turf through the API, only toggle active. If intended, OK; else expose a soft-delete endpoint.
Now 1476 lines (was 1441). Still above the 700-line split threshold flagged in iterations 1-3. Not addressed.
Still deprecated FastAPI on_event (carry-over from iter-1/2/3).

action_items: (New, LOW) Sniff file magic bytes in upload_media instead of trusting Content-Type; also cap number of files per request.
(Carry-over) Modularize server.py (1476 LOC) and migrate on_event to lifespan handlers.
(Carry-over from iter-3) Fix controlled→uncontrolled React warnings in PayoutMethodCard (not re-tested this run).
critical_code_review_comments: serve_media correctly restricts to the goturf/turfs/ prefix and rejects '..', keeping verification docs private — good separation from /files.

upload_media stores objects under goturf/turfs/{owner_id}/<uuid>.<ext>, which is a nice per-owner namespace, but there is no server-side ownership check on serve_media; any owner's media is readable by anyone (that's intended for public turf photos, just confirm product intent).

The frontend builds absolute URLs via `${BACKEND_URL}${url}` and stores them in turf.images. If BACKEND_URL ever changes (preview vs. prod), all existing turf.images rows become dead links. Consider storing the relative path and resolving at render time.
Content-Type gate uses the client-provided MIME; combine with filename extension validation and server-side sniffing to prevent SVG/XSS or disguised uploads.
No image dimension / aspect / content moderation on uploads — fine for MVP, worth flagging for a future iteration (ClamAV + a moderation step for public media).
